subject: POC fast-start: success metrics, timeline, and model shortlist
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@brightroute.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC fast-start: success metrics, timeline, and model shortlist

Hi Carlos / Elena —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a concrete proposal for a 4–6 week fast-start POC so we can (a) validate accuracy across Spanish/French, (b) measure latency and cost at scale, and (c) verify integration points for your payments support flow.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary business goal: automated triage + assistant for merchant dispute classification and enrichment (pre-populated fields for the payments ops team).
- Volume expectation: ~1M prompts/month initially, bursty during EOD processing windows.
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 300ms for token streaming in endpoint mode (we discussed 200–300ms range).
- Data / compliance: EU data residency required for PII logs; SOC2/alignment required (you mentioned a security questionnaire).
- Languages: EN + high-quality Spanish & French in scope for the POC.

Proposed POC success criteria (suggested measurable thresholds):
1) Accuracy: intent classification F1 >= 0.87 on your labeled set (sample size ~2k).
2) Entity extraction: field extraction exact match >= 85% on sample dataset.
3) Latency: 95th percentile per-request <= 300ms under production-like load (50 RPS sustained).
4) Cost: per-1000-token cost < target budget (we'll estimate after model mapping).
5) Reliability: end-to-end availability >= 99% during the test window.

High-level evaluation plan and timeline (fast-start / lightweight):
- Week 0 (this week): SOW + account access & dataset drop (you host/sftp or share Drive link).
- Week 1: Kickoff, infra provisioning (Redwood sandbox dedicated pool), ingest sample dataset, baseline runs.
- Week 2: Model shortlist testing (benchmarks for latency, cost, and quality on holdout set).
- Weeks 3–4: Fine-tune / LoRA experiments (if needed) and A/B evaluation with your metrics.
- Week 5: Production-like load test + final metric review.
- Week 6: Acceptance review and playbook for rollout.

Model shortlist (initial recommendation — we will validate in Week 2):
- Primary candidate: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized + Redwood runtime optimizations) — best balance for multilingual accuracy with a single model.
- Cost-focused candidate: Mistral-instruct-7B (lower inference cost; evaluate Spanish/French quality vs. Llama).
- Fallback: Llama-2-7B-quant (aggressive quantization) for latency-sensitive burst windows, with automatic routing to primary when accuracy confidence is high.

Redwood ops notes: we will enable prefix/KV caching for repeated merchant prompts, continuous batching for throughput, and guardrail policies to fallback models when latency or quota thresholds hit. We'll also instrument token-level cost traces so you can see dollars per-route.

Attachments: poc-checklist.pdf (kickoff checklist), trial-sla-draft.docx (proposed trial terms).

Ask: please confirm the success criteria above and whether you can do a kickoff week of June 14th. Also confirm preferred dataset delivery mechanism (SFTP or shared Drive) and the internal owner for dataset approvals.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
m: +1 415 555 0198

From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@brightroute.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Martins <elena@brightroute.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 11:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: POC fast-start: success metrics, timeline, and model shortlist

Markus —

Appreciate the clear recap and the proposed timeline. Quick responses / clarifications from our side:
- We can confirm kickoff week of June 14th.
- Dataset delivery: we prefer a shared Drive link for the initial drop (contains redacted PII). I will share read-only access to the "BR_Sandbox_POC" folder by end of day.
- Languages: Spanish (ES) is critical; French (FR) is "nice-to-have" but we'd like to see both in the Week 2 benchmark.
- Volume: 1M prompts/month is correct; bursts can reach ~120 RPS for short windows.
- Latency: 300ms 95p is our internal target for the assist flow. If we can get closer to 200ms for the high-priority path that's ideal.
- Compliance: we'll send the security questionnaire (SOC2 items) and a short redlines pdf for your trial SLA.

Cost: pricing will be a material factor for us. Can you include a provisional per-1k-token cost estimate for each shortlisted model in Week 2 so we can map to a 12-month run-rate?

Owner: I'm the internal owner for the POC (Carlos Ruiz). Elena (cc'ed) is the lead product manager and will own dataset approvals.

Attached: brightroute-requirements-redlines.pdf (contains a couple contract asks).

Thanks,
Carlos
Head of Integrations | BrightRoute Payments

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC fast-start: success metrics, timeline, and model shortlist

Folks —

Nice recap Markus. A few operational notes and owners so we can move quickly:

Proposed model mapping (benchmarks we'll run Week 2):
- Llama-2-13B-chat: primary model for multilingual quality. We'll run 8-bit quantized baseline and an INT4 candidate via our quantized runtime. Expect better Spanish performance vs small 7B models.
- Mistral-instruct-7B: cost-efficient contender. Good single-pass instruction performance; we'll validate FR/ES quality.
- Llama-2-7B-quant: aggressive low-cost fallback for burst windows. Use routing policy to send low-confidence/low-entity requests to the primary model.

Ownership / responsibilities:
- Solutions & infra: Markus to provision Redwood sandbox and run initial baselines (deadline: Jun 18).
- Eval & metrics: Priyom to own metric collection, A/B test harness, and dataset scoring (deadline: Ongoing, summary by Jun 25).
- Commercial & SOW: Marissa to prepare the trial SOW and pricing slides (deadline: Jun 10 draft).
- Customer comms: Ben will be primary AE for contract questions; Markus remains technical lead.

Instrumentation we will enable by default:
- Token-level cost traces and per-route latency breakdowns in the console.
- Confidence scoring + model fallback logs for audit.

Marissa: can you prepare a lightweight pricing sketch (per 1k tokens for each model) to share with Carlos after we have the Week 2 benchmark numbers? He asked for a provisional estimate.

Next steps: Markus to confirm sandbox details + Drive link once Carlos shares access. Recommend a brief 30-min kickoff on Jun 14 (calendar invite after SOW sign).

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@brightroute.com>, Elena Martins <elena@brightroute.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC fast-start: success metrics, timeline, and model shortlist

Carlos / Elena —

Great — thank you for the quick confirmation and for committing to the Drive share. Finalizing logistics on our end:

1) Kickoff call: proposed Tue Jun 15 10:00 AM CEST (Jun 14 slot was US-centric; moved to accommodate your EMEA team). Please confirm.
2) Access: once you grant the "BR_Sandbox_POC" Drive folder, we will drop a short ingestion checklist and a pre-signed SFTP option if needed.
3) Owners recap: Carlos (Customer POC Owner), Elena (Dataset approver), Markus (Redwood technical lead), Priyom (Eval & metrics), Marissa (SOW/pricing), Ben (commercial).
4) Attachments: I've attached the poc-checklist.pdf and trial-sla-draft.docx again for easy reference in the kickoff invite.

Action items for BrightRoute before kickoff:
- Share Drive access to sample datasets (required).
- Complete and return the security questionnaire (we'll send via secure DocuSign link).
- Confirm acceptance of the POC success criteria or propose adjustments in reply by EOD Jun 12.

After kickoff we'll run a quick baseline against each candidate model and share a short deck with quality vs latency vs cost trade-offs. Marissa will send the SOW draft today; Ben will follow up on any commercial redlines.

Looking forward — we'll get calendar invites out once Carlos confirms the time.

Best,
Markus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
